text: Given the code at src/mcp-server.ts:119-156, confirmed by inspection that every register*Tools call -- including the five new tools -- receives the same per-request client as every existing tool, with no module-level/shared client instance in the five new tool registrations
steps: Confirm registerServiceTools(server, client) and registerTimeEntryTools(server, client) are called with the single locally-scoped client built from configOverride ?? getConfig() for that invocation
Confirm the five new tools added inside service.ts/time-entries.ts take client as a function parameter from registerServiceTools/registerTimeEntryTools, not an import of a shared singleton
expect: No new tool reads credentials from anywhere other than the client parameter passed into its register*Tools call
evidence: Code inspection, 2026-10-23: src/mcp-server.ts:156 builds `const client = new CwManageClient(config)` once per createMcpServer() invocation; src/mcp-server.ts:162 calls registerTimeEntryTools(server, client) and :166 calls registerServiceTools(server, client) with that same per-invocation client. The five new tools (cw_list_ticket_types/subtypes/items in src/tools/service.ts, cw_list_work_types/cw_list_work_roles in src/tools/time-entries.ts) are defined inside those same registerXTools(server, client) function bodies and close over that `client` parameter -- confirmed via `grep -n "^import" src/tools/service.ts src/tools/time-entries.ts`: both files import only zod, the McpServer type, and the CwManageClient type, no module-level client instance. No live two-credential integration harness exists in this environment, so this remains a code-review check rather than a live multi-tenant call, same caveat as the original design.
